title: Constructive Lean 4 Kernel and Exact Zero-Float Certificates for Google Research Cogentic's Sub-Quasi-Polynomial Discrete Logarithm Proof
abstract: A November 25, 2026 preprint from Google Research's Cogentic system proposes an unconditional classical zero-error Las Vegas algorithm for the Discrete Logarithm Problem (DLP) in F_{p^n}^x of fixed characteristic p with claimed expected runtime exp((2+o(1))/ln(ln(ln n)) * (ln n)^2) = (p^n)^{o(log n)}, improving upon the (p^n)^{Theta(log n)} barrier of Kleinjung-Wesolowski and Lido. Rather than assuming peer-reviewed validation of its analytic pillars, we deliver an independent, explicitly scoped, zero-floating-point verification companion for its deterministic algebraic, elliptic-Lang, linearized-monodromy, and factoring-free unimodular mechanisms. Layer 1 (CogenticDiscreteLog.lean) proves 18 standalone constructive Lean 4.35.0 algebraic, inductive, and arithmetic sub-lemmas (zero sorry, zero axiom, zero Classical.choice, zero warnings; 1 zero-axiom, 2 [propext], and 15 [propext, Quot.sound]). Layer 2 (DLP-COGENTIC-CERT-1.0) is a pure-stdlib Python int auditor across four modes that certifies 16 canonical finite witnesses in 1.133-36.640 ms—including live exact Lang-isogeny equations phi_q(I_0) = I_0 + Q across p in {2,3,5,7}, Moore/affine-Moore pencils with complete splitting, and factoring-free SL_2(Z) solves modulo unfactored composites up to M_L = 406,901—and rejects 61/61 live adversarial forgeries with exact branch assertions (65/65 pytest checks).
